close_reason:
Moved ChatCapability and ChatPushCapability from chat-client/session.rs to chat-types/src/capability.rs. Added JMAP_CHAT_URI and JMAP_CHAT_PUSH_URI consts. BodyType wire-format enum also moved from chat-client/types.rs to chat-types/src/message.rs (alongside DeliveryState/ReadDisposition) since ChatCapability.supported_body_types references it. chat-client now re-exports BodyType, ChatCapability, ChatPushCapability from chat-types; call sites updated.

This eliminates the wrong-direction dependency (chat-server can now import ChatCapability without depending on chat-client) and brings chat-types into line with the 6 sibling extension-types crates (calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing, metadata) that already host their capability surface in *-types.

Capability structs retain the workspace extras-preservation 'extra' field they had in chat-client (this is the OPPOSITE choice from ops7.6 where mail-types capability structs do NOT carry extra — see ops7.6 close comment). The chat case preserves the existing behavior of the moved structs to keep the move surgical; whether all capability structs should adopt extras is a separate workspace-architectural decision. Filing-and-continuing rather than reshaping extras during a move.

Workspace cargo test, cargo clippy, and rustdoc are all clean. 5 new capability tests + 2 new BodyType tests pass, using hand-built JSON fixtures with independent oracles.

URI-const adoption in chat-client itself (replacing the hardcoded 'urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat' strings in USING_CHAT / primary_account_id sites) is in scope of follow-up bd:JMAP-ops7.16, not this bead.
description:
**Files**:
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/session.rs:38 — \`pub struct ChatCapability { ... }\`
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/session.rs:114 — \`pub struct ChatPushCapability { ... }\`
- crate-jmap-chat-types/src/ — NO capability struct, NO URI const

**Divergence**: 6 of 8 extension type crates expose capability struct(s) + URI const(s) in their *-types crate (calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing, metadata). chat is the only extension whose capability struct lives outside its types crate — it's defined in chat-client/session.rs, which means:
1. chat-server cannot import \`ChatCapability\` without depending on chat-client (an upside-down dependency direction).
2. Any third-party consumer that builds a session response server-side has to redefine \`ChatCapability\` from scratch or hardcode the JSON shape.
3. The URI string \`urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat\` is referenced via doc comments and string literals in 3 different files (chat-server/src/backend.rs:151, chat-client/src/lib.rs, chat-client/src/session.rs) — no single source of truth.

mail-types has the same omission (no \`MailCapability\` / \`MailAccountCapability\` / \`JMAP_MAIL_URI\` — see separate finding) but mail's RFC 8621 capability is non-trivial (with \`maxMailboxesPerEmail\`, \`maxMailboxDepth\`, etc.) whereas chat's two capabilities are simple structs that fit comfortably in chat-types alongside the other 35 chat wire types.

**What goes wrong**:
1. Today: chat-server has no shared capability type to advertise in a session-response builder. Sibling extension servers (e.g. calendars-server) can use \`jmap_calendars_types::CalendarsAccountCapability\` directly.
2. Tomorrow: when a workspace consumer (kith, stoa, jmapchat-server reference impl) needs the URI const for routing or session-builder logic, they have nothing to import from chat-types and must hardcode the URI string.

**Fix**: move \`ChatCapability\` and \`ChatPushCapability\` from chat-client/session.rs to chat-types/src/capability.rs. Add \`pub const JMAP_CHAT_URI: &str = "urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat";\` and \`pub const JMAP_CHAT_PUSH_URI: &str = "urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:push";\`. Re-export from chat-client for backward compat.

Sibling reference: crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/capability.rs is the canonical layout.
title: chat-types lacks `ChatCapability` struct and `JMAP_CHAT_URI` const; `ChatCapability` lives in chat-client (wrong dependency direction)
